input: Design a custom cross-stitch pattern from a photo

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The photo subject (portrait, pet, landscape, logo) heavily affects how the design is simplified and which details can realistically be preserved in stitch form.

The finished stitch size and canvas count (e.g. 14-count Aida) determine the pattern's grid resolution — a small hoop with high count gives fine detail, a large hoop with low count gives a bolder, simpler look.
Knowing who will stitch this — a beginner or an experienced stitcher — determines acceptable complexity, number of thread colors, and pattern annotation style.
The desired color palette approach (photo-realistic DMC colors vs. stylized/limited palette) completely changes the conversion method and the final aesthetic.
Whether the user wants a printable PDF chart, a digital file for software (like Pattern Keeper), or a physical kit affects the deliverable and tools needed.
The intended use — framed wall art, a gift, a hoop to keep — affects finishing decisions and how much border or negative space should be built into the pattern.
Knowing whether the priority is a close likeness to the photo vs. a clean, easy-to-stitch graphic determines how aggressively the image is simplified during conversion.

gold.taskTitle: Design a custom cross-stitch pattern from a photo
gold.taskDescription: Convert a personal photo into a stitchable cross-stitch pattern, which involves decisions about design translation, materials, sizing, and intended output format.

questions.title: What is the subject of the photo being used?
questions.description: Identify whether the photo is a portrait, pet, landscape, object, or graphic, as this determines how detail is preserved and where simplification is applied during pattern conversion.

questions.title: What finished size and fabric count do you have in mind?
questions.description: Establish the target stitch dimensions and Aida/evenweave count (e.g. 6x6 inches on 14-count), which sets the grid resolution and level of achievable detail.

questions.title: Who will be stitching this — a beginner or experienced stitcher?
questions.description: Determine the skill level of the person stitching to calibrate pattern complexity, number of thread colors, and how heavily the chart is annotated.

questions.title: Should the colors stay photo-realistic or follow a simplified palette?
questions.description: Clarify whether the pattern should use a full range of DMC thread colors to closely match the photo, or be reduced to a limited, stylized set of colors for a cleaner look.

questions.title: What format do you need the finished pattern in?
questions.description: Determine whether the deliverable should be a printable PDF chart, a digital file compatible with stitching apps like Pattern Keeper, or another format.

questions.title: What is this cross-stitch piece ultimately going to be used for?
questions.description: Understand the intended end use — framed art, a gift, a functional item — so the pattern can account for appropriate borders, negative space, and finishing requirements.

questions.title: Is a close likeness to the photo or easy stitchability the top priority?
questions.description: Establish the primary success criterion so the right balance is struck between photographic accuracy and a clean, manageable pattern during the image-to-grid conversion.
